source.title: Double Descent for Random Fourier Series Models
source.authors: Hang-Rong Xu; Yi Shen; Yu-Zhong Zhao

record.tranche_reason: The study directly analyzes and simulates double descent, using random partial DFT regression rather than deep networks.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own theoretical risk formulas and numerical risk curves. Results cited from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study derives exact risk formulas and simulates risk curves for least-squares regression with random partial DFT matrices, a non-deep model class. It reports a peak at p=n and a second descent for p>n, which bears directly on V4, and through the formulas on V3 and V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude that, without noise, the over-parameterized optimum always beats the under-parameterized one. With noise, the better regime depends on σ and ρn, and at large noise the under-parameterized model may be preferable. They describe the prescient-selection curve as resembling tempered overfitting.
record.recipe_differences: Uses random partial DFT linear regression and isotropic random coefficients, derives risk formulas with random-matrix tools, and includes Gaussian observation noise; it does not study deep networks.
record.method_sensitivity: Risk depends on the parameter and sample ratios and, in noisy settings, on σ²; the authors also report different curve shapes for random versus prescient feature selection.
record.problems: Numerical curves are presented as plots without reported error bars or confidence intervals; simulations use 50 realizations and D=512 or 1024. The numerical signal is chosen once per plot, while the theoretical risk averages over β and noise.
record.rows_left_out: Figures 2 and 3 are not duplicated beyond the sample-ratio result recorded in r6; Figure 2 fixes ρn=1 and is not a separate test of the listed claim versions. The cited findings from prior work are excluded.

untested.parts: No explicit sample-ratio sweep at fixed interior ρp<1, and no simulation of one. Only ρp=1 is plotted.
Only one model class (random partial DFT least squares); no other model classes.
No effective-complexity measure predicting peak location.
No regularization, no optimally tuned ridge, no triple or multiple descent, no label noise.

missing.what: Phase transition in (σ², ρn): for σ≥1 the under-parameterized minimum (1, at ρp→0) is below the over-parameterized minimum 1+(σ²−1)ρn. For σ<1 there is an interior minimizer ρp*.
Sample-wise risk at fixed interior ρp implied by Theorem 2, which diverges as ρn→ρp. It is not stated or plotted by the authors.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche set to T3 rather than T2: the study is a new model-class setting for V4, closely following Belkin, Hsu and Xu (2020), which is not an original source here. The V6 label in the record cited the noiseless rows r4 and r5, which are not linked to V6; the noiseless evidence is now carried by r2 via Corollary 1. Simulations draw β once per plot and report no error bars.

versions.untested_parts: Deep networks and model-size double descent specifically in deep networks.
Risk over training epochs or training time.
The study varies sample ratio with p/D=1, but does not test more samples raising risk near an interior interpolation threshold.
The study tests a random Fourier series regression model, not a range of model classes.
A single effective-complexity measure predicting peak location across axes.
The study varies Gaussian observation-noise levels, but does not isolate noise from signal variance as the cause of the peak, test triple or multiple descent, or test optimally tuned regularization.
Recounting complexity using an effective number of parameters.

rows.subject: random partial DFT Fourier series regression model
rows.size_stated: D, n, p → ∞ with ρn and ρp fixed
rows.operation_detail: Asymptotic risk as the parameter ratio ρp varies below the sample ratio ρn
rows.measure: Conditional expected squared coefficient error Ee,β[||β−β̂||² | S,T]
rows.note: The risk expression describes the under-parameterized branch; the authors characterize it as strictly convex in ρp for fixed ρn.
rows.check: Under-parameterized branch only. Per Remark 3, for ρn≤1/2 (and for σ≥1) the minimum is at ρp→0, so there is no first descent and the classical U-shape is degenerate. Partial is correct.

rows.subject: random partial DFT Fourier series regression model
rows.size_stated: D, n, p → ∞ with ρn and ρp fixed
rows.operation_detail: Asymptotic risk at the interpolation threshold
rows.measure: Conditional expected squared coefficient error Ee,β[||β−β̂||² | S,T]
rows.note: The theorem states almost-sure divergence at equal sampling ratios.
rows.check: Add V3: the divergence at ρp=ρn also holds when ρp is fixed and ρn rises to meet it. The divergence holds for every σ, including σ=0 (Corollary 1).

rows.subject: random partial DFT Fourier series regression model
rows.size_stated: D, n, p → ∞ with ρn and ρp fixed
rows.operation_detail: Asymptotic risk as the parameter ratio ρp varies above the sample ratio ρn
rows.measure: Conditional expected squared coefficient error Ee,β[||β−β̂||² | S,T]
rows.note: For fixed ρn, the authors state this over-parameterized risk is strictly decreasing in ρp.
rows.check: Add V3: for fixed ρp the over-parameterized formula rises with ρn toward the threshold. Example: ρp=0.5 gives 1.025 at ρn=0.1 and 1.133 at ρn=0.2. This is derived from the formula; the authors do not state it.

relationships.condition: Fixed ρp<1, ρn increasing toward ρp (Theorem 2, over-parameterized branch)
relationships.reason: The formula rises with ρn and diverges at ρn=ρp (r2, r3). This is derived from the theorem, not stated or plotted by the authors.
relationships.display_finding: The theorem's formula implies risk rises with ρn and diverges at ρn=ρp.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Fixed ρp<1, ρn increasing toward ρp (Theorem 2, over-parameterized branch)
source_check.reason: For fixed interior ρp, the formula increases sufficiently near ρn=ρp and diverges there. This is an analytical implication, not an empirical sample sweep; monotonic increase over the entire branch is not guaranteed.

relationships.reason: Risk is 1−ρn, strictly decreasing in samples, with no harm near ρn=1 (r6).
relationships.display_finding: Risk equals 1−ρn and decreases strictly with samples, including near ρn=1.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: Corollary 2 and Remark 4 give risk 1−ρn, decreasing throughout this boundary setting; the interior sample-wise divergence does not extend to all retained coordinates.

relationships.condition: Random partial DFT regression, ρp>ρn, noiseless and noisy (σ from 0.01 to 10), random and prescient selection
relationships.reason: Risk diverges at ρp=ρn and strictly decreases for ρp>ρn (r2, r3). Simulations show the peak and second descent (r4, r5, r7, r8–r17).
relationships.display_finding: With random selection, risk diverged at ρp = ρn and strictly decreased for ρp > ρn with or without observation noise; noiseless prescient-selection simulations also showed a peak and second descent.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Random partial DFT regression, ρp>ρn, noiseless and noisy (σ from 0.01 to 10), random and prescient selection
source_check.reason: Support holds with narrower conditions: random selection is analyzed and simulated with and without observation noise; prescient selection is simulated only without noise in Figure 5. The isotropic random-selection formulas do not establish divergence or strict monotonicity for noisy prescient selection.

relationships.reason: The first descent is degenerate: the best under-parameterized risk is at ρp→0, so there is no classical U-shape (r1, r4, r5). A full curve appears only with prescient selection (r7).
relationships.display_finding: For ρn ≤ 1/2, the best underparameterized risk occurred as ρp → 0, eliminating the classical U-shape; a full curve required prescient selection.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: Remark 3 places the under-parameterized optimum at ρp→0 in this regime. Section 5 explicitly describes the first descent as degenerate, qualifying the classical U-shaped portion.

relationships.reason: Per Remark 3 (text), the over-parameterized minimum 1+(σ²−1)ρn can exceed the under-parameterized minimum of 1. The second descent then does not beat the classical regime (r1, r3).
relationships.display_finding: The overparameterized minimum was 1 + (σ² − 1)ρn, equaling the underparameterized minimum of 1 at σ = 1 and exceeding it for σ > 1.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: V4 requires risk to improve as capacity increases past interpolation, which Remark 3 proves even at large noise. It does not require outperforming the best under-parameterized model. The minima are equal at σ=1; the over-parameterized minimum exceeds 1 for σ>1.

relationships.condition: Gaussian observation noise σ=0 to 10, no regularization
relationships.reason: The peak diverges at ρp=ρn for every σ, including σ=0 (r2, Corollary 1), so observation noise is not needed for the peak. σ² only scales the variance term (r1, r3, r8–r17).
relationships.display_finding: The peak diverges at ρp = ρn throughout σ = 0 to 10, while σ² scales the variance term.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Gaussian observation noise σ=0 to 10, no regularization
source_check.reason: The formulas support the noise/variance component: σ² amplifies the divergent spectral term, whose coefficient remains positive at σ=0. A noiseless peak does not contradict a claim allowing variance as its driver. Multiple peaks and optimally tuned regularization are untested.
